status: INTERIM (Phase A complete: ETTh1 H96 + H720, seed0 only; Phase B (Weather) not yet run)

ETTh1_H96.pattern: D increases meaningfully, C essentially flat (noisy, no clear decrease) -- does NOT match the section-20 success pattern

ETTh1_H720.pattern: D nearly constant, C clearly and monotonically decreases -- MATCHES the section-20 success pattern (D approx const, C down, Agg down, Forecast down)

ETTh1_H96.note: overlap rises very fast with S -- slots are largely redundant by S=4

ETTh1_H720.note: overlap stays low and rises slowly with S -- slots remain meaningfully differentiated even at S=10

case_assessment.ETTh1_H720: Case A -- Multi-Slot effect present: S>1 consistently and significantly improves Stage1 AggMSE AND Stage2 forecast MSE, monotonically in S, via the D-const/C-down mechanism.
case_assessment.ETTh1_H96: Fits neither Case A, B, C, nor D cleanly. Not Case B (slot collapse) in the strict sense -- forecast at S2 is significantly WORSE than S1, not merely 'no different'. Not Case C -- C does not decrease at all (stays flat/noisy), only D worsens. Closest description: slots DO specialize by S=4 (per overlap stats) but that specialization does not translate into complementarity gains at this horizon -- specialization without benefit, plus a small individual-relevance cost.

rq_answers.RQ1_multislot_improves_retrieval_alone: Horizon-dependent: YES at H720 (Stage1 AggMSE significantly better, monotonic in S), NO at H96 (Stage1 AggMSE significantly WORSE for every S>1).
rq_answers.RQ2_increasing_s_reduces_c: YES at H720 (monotonic, -3.3% relative at S10 vs S1, all vs-S1 comparisons except S2 significant). NO at H96 (C is flat/noisy, no monotonic decrease, no significant improvement at any S).
rq_answers.RQ3_c_reduction_without_sacrificing_d: At H720: YES -- D changes only +1.8% relative while C changes -3.3%, a clean asymmetric D-const/C-down pattern. (Not applicable at H96 since C never decreases there.)
rq_answers.RQ4_improved_set_quality_transfers_to_fo: YES at H720 -- Stage1 AggMSE and Stage2 forecast MSE improve together, monotonically in S, both significant from S4 onward. Consistent (null) at H96 -- neither improves.
rq_answers.RQ5_is_s10_necessary: At H720, S10 gives the single best Stage1 AND Stage2 result of all arms tested, better than S4 -- marginal gain from S4->S10 (-0.0026 stage2) is smaller than S1->S4 (-0.0045), suggesting diminishing but not yet fully saturated returns; S=10 not shown to be strictly necessary vs. S=4, but is not wasteful either. At H96 the question is moot (no arm beats S1 significantly).
rq_answers.RQ6_effect_stronger_at_h720_than_h96: YES, unambiguously -- this is the track's central finding, replicating the same horizon-dependence pattern TRACK-R/TRACK-S already observed for the full M2 method, now shown to arise from the Multi-Slot architecture in ISOLATION (no StopGrad-Key, no overlap penalty, no aggregate loss, no relevance budget).
rq_answers.RQ7_transfers_eth1_to_weather: NOT YET TESTED -- Phase B (Weather H96/H720 seed0) has not been run.

part_30_final_question.question: Does giving Original-future-aligned-KL retrieval multiple independent query slots, alone, improve set complementarity and forecasting?
part_30_final_question.answer: YES at H720, NO (mildly negative) at H96 -- the answer to the track's core question is itself horizon-dependent on the one dataset tested so far. This is a genuine, mechanistically-explained (D-const/C-down at H720; D-up/C-flat at H96) effect of num_slots in isolation, not an artifact of StopGrad-Key/overlap/aggregate/budget terms (none of which are present in this track).

stop_rule_compliance: No StopGrad, overlap penalty, aggregate loss, relevance budget, slot-specific teacher, or slot-count fine-tuning added anywhere in this track, despite the H96 negative-ish result. Reported honestly as-is per PART 25/26.
next_step: Phase B: Weather H96 seed0 and Weather H720 seed0, identical protocol, no hyperparameter changes.
